hook_text: We've looked at the Moon for thousands of years, and never seen its other side. Why?
clip_script: Ladysmith Moon diaries. Thin crescent, half moon, full moon, and back again: one month. But the dark patches never move! Try this: walk around a chair while you keep facing it. One trip around, and you've turned around once yourself. The Moon does the same: it spins once in about 28 days as it circles the Earth. Same face, every night. And the whole time, the Earth and Moon travel around the Sun together.
visual_style: Whiteboard Moon diary page, then a top view of a learner walking around a chair, then the Earth and Moon circling a lamp.
mood: Curious and playful, solving a sky mystery.
pacing: Diary pages flick by, then a slow walk around the chair.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and keep your own Moon diary for a week.
